evidence: Plan: 'Trigger full replication for remote `github`; this trigger/backfill is the mechanism that creates any missing refs'
infra/gerrit/setup-replication.sh:14 'REMOTE PLUGIN ADMIN IS DISABLED on this instance'; lines 101-117 gate `plugin reload`/admin SSH behind ALLOW_REMOTE_RELOAD (default 0)
infra/gerrit/replication.config:53 `replicateOnStartup = false` — a restart does not auto-trigger a full sweep
infra/gerrit/setup-replication.sh:52 documents the trigger form `replication start --all --remote github --now --wait` (runs over admin SSH)
findings.finding: The plan's 'Trigger full replication for remote github' step is the load-bearing external capability (the AC requires 'full replication has been triggered successfully'), but it names no mechanism and does not reconcile the disabled-remote-admin precondition the repo documents. The repo's setup-replication.sh states REMOTE PLUGIN ADMIN IS DISABLED on this instance (ALLOW_REMOTE_RELOAD default 0) and replication.config sets replicateOnStartup=false, so a restart alone will not replicate; the documented trigger form `replication start --all --remote github --now --wait` runs over admin SSH, which is the disabled capability. Whether the trigger is achievable as described is therefore UNVERIFIED.
findings.location: Plan > 'Trigger full replication for remote github'; AC line 'The live Gerrit host has the updated replication config applied and full replication has been triggered successfully.'
findings.suggested_fix: Update the trigger step to cite the repo-documented command `replication start --all --remote github --now --wait` and note it requires enabling admin SSH (ALLOW_REMOTE_RELOAD=1) since remote plugin admin is disabled by default and replicateOnStartup=false means a restart will not backfill on its own.

ADR-0021 line 27-31: 'Replication lag is tolerated by a fallback, not a hard dependency. checkout-gerrit-change-action fetches ... from the GitHub mirror first and falls back to fetching directly from the Gerrit server ... if the ref hasn't replicated yet.'
ADR-0010 lines 27-32: NON-force refspecs are 'the one-way door - the only safe way GitHub state changes is a fast-forward'

findings.finding: The plan adopts a FORCE refspec `+refs/changes/*:refs/changes/*` without justifying it against the established NON-force approach the repo already documents for the same failure class. ADR-0021 handles replication lag/misses via the checkout-gerrit-change-action gerrit-url fallback plus triggering replication (both of which this plan already performs), and the plan's own RCA plus operator ruling concede the diagnosed cause was a MISSING ref that 'the force ... is not what creates.' Prior art (ADR-0010/0021) treats NON-force as the core safety property, so switching to force is a departure that needs an explicit anti-repackaging / Rule-of-Three justification of what the force adds beyond the existing fallback+trigger remedy.
findings.location: Operator ruling + Plan bullet 'Update only the Gerrit change-ref replication spec to ... `+refs/changes/*:refs/changes/*`'
